 Marshall Faulk enjoys Trey Holly in the present, sees his bright future
 November 12, 2026
 Posted by: Ro Brown
 Category: College Football , Southern 
 Southern University running back Trey Holly must feel like he’s back in high school.
 It was at Union Parish High School in Farmerville, Louisiana, where Holly obliterated the state’s career rushing record by nearly 2,000 yards, piling up 10,523 yards in four seasons.
 The redshirt junior is on a tear this season, rushing for 1,239 yards and 11 touchdowns with two games remaining on the schedule. He leads the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC) in both categories while averaging 5.8 yards per carry.
 “I’m proud that he trusted me and the advice that I gave him when I took over the program. And now, he’s seeing the fruits of his labor,” says Jaguars head coach Marshall Faulk.
 Those aren’t the words of an obviously biased coach campaigning for postseason honors for one of his players.
 The coach is one of the greatest running backs of all time.
 A Pro Football Hall of Famer.
 A Super Bowl champion.
 Marshall Faulk knows a running back when he sees one. Trey Holly would be wise to follow the advice of one of the best to ever play the position.
 “The kid is phenomenal on and off the field. He’s not only raised his level of play, but he’s raised his level of leadership and holding guys accountable, not by words but by his actions.”
 Faulk added, “He shows up not just on time but early. He’s doing the little things that people may not see, but his peers are watching.”
 Holly put together a solid sophomore season on The Bluff, rushing for 798 yards on 121 carries in eight games in 2025. That performance, however, didn’t exactly impress the first-year head coach, who made sure Holly knew it.
 “He was the best player on a bad team. That’s easy. I challenged him that you have to get better at everything. And I nit-picked him at everything he did.”
 Faulk admits Holly was a lot like Marshall Faulk the player during the formative years of his career. He had to try things his way before being willing to listen to the coach.
 Combine the realization that his way might not be the best way with his God-given abilities, and the result is a player who has produced three 200-yard rushing performances this season: 200 against Louisiana Christian, 204 against Florida A&M and 206 against Bethune-Cookman.
 “He has the ability to run low, his ability to run behind his pads. His center of gravity and the ability to run inside and outside. The toughness to run somebody over and the speed to run away from people.”
 “This kid will play high-level football!!!”
 At 5-foot-7 and 192 pounds, Holly also had to take better care of his body. The results are showing on the field.
 Faulk points to Holly’s performance in the late stages of games this season as evidence of his improved conditioning and commitment.
 “All the fancy stuff, the dressing, you do that in the beginning of the games. At the end of the games, you close it out with hard-nosed, tough football. Trey has responded and he’s taking care of his body and doing the things necessary to continue to be effective.”
 In this day and age of Name, Image and Likeness (NIL), Faulk is realistic about Holly’s future as a collegiate athlete.
 “There’s no doubt he will be in the portal, and somebody will be paying him. If he doesn’t play another down for us, his resume is what it is.”
 Southern is currently 5-5, with games remaining against Alcorn State and archrival Grambling in the Bayou Classic.
 Holly is enjoying the best season by a Southern ballcarrier since Lenard Tillery’s All-American campaign in 2015. Tillery rushed for 1,665 yards that season and remains the SWAC’s all-time rushing leader with 4,857 career yards.
 Holly may not reach Tillery’s single-season or career marks. It’s also possible he won’t be at Southern for his senior season.
 But Faulk isn’t shy about where Trey Holly stands in his estimation.
 “He’s the best back in this state or any southern state right now.”
